# SasaVenos Says Variation Should Be Done While Respecting Specificity

SasaVenos says that variation should be done while respecting specificity, and that if you have been doing the same exercise for a long time and cannot make progress, you can replace it with a similar exercise to add variety. [src: vid-BBuB0XMVhDw]

## Details

- When you do the same kind of training and the same exercise over and over, the muscles and the nervous system get used to it over time, making it harder to get better. [src: vid-BBuB0XMVhDw]
- Variation should be done while respecting specificity. [src: vid-BBuB0XMVhDw]
- If you have been doing weighted pull-ups since forever and cannot make progress with them anymore, you can replace them with chin-ups to add some variety. [src: vid-BBuB0XMVhDw]
- It is important to stick to the new exercise for a decent amount of time because your body needs to forget the old exercise so that you are potentiated to make better gains once you reintroduce it. [src: vid-BBuB0XMVhDw]

## Evidence

- vid-BBuB0XMVhDw (SasaVenos): "when you do the same kind of training, the same exercise over and over, not only it gets kind of boring after a while, but it also appears that the muscles and the nervous system gets used to it over time, and they make it harder to get better."
- vid-BBuB0XMVhDw (SasaVenos): "Variation should be done while respecting specificity."
- vid-BBuB0XMVhDw (SasaVenos): "If you've been doing weighted pull-ups since forever and you can't seem to make progress with them anymore, you can replace them with chin-ups to add some variety."
- vid-BBuB0XMVhDw (SasaVenos): "No matter what you choose to do, it's important to stick to the new exercise for a decent amount of time. That is because your body needs to kind of forget the old exercise so that you're potentiated to make better gains once you reintroduce it, because it's much more sensitive again."
